genre: narrative prose — characters named by role (Kafka's Metamorphosis, the motivating case), with titled named entities so the referents type as persons
note: A synthetic Metamorphosis scene. Hand-annotated coreference gold for the role-referent overlay (PR2). The named characters carry titles ('Miss Grete', 'Mrs. Samsa') so the entity reader types them as persons and learns gender from the title (name-anchored, not a sentence window). Each role recurs past the mention floor and co-occurs with its true referent. The four discriminating verdicts: his sister binds Grete and his mother binds Mrs. Samsa (gender agreement from the role head + co-occurrence); his father is standalone (Kafka never names him — the possessor exclusion: a role is not its own possessor); the lodgers is standalone (the plural number veto — a plural role cannot be a single named person). The chief clerk is standalone (the protagonist hub, its only co-occurrent, is excluded as the maximal-cooccurrence party).
